section: Transport in India - inland waterways, shipping, major and minor ports, civil aviation
subsections: Major ports → state, coast and speciality

accepted.s: As per the current classification of major ports, which one of the following is the 13th major port of India?
accepted.x: Vadhavan, approved on 19 June 2024, is counted as the 13th major port along with the 12 operational major ports. Older references that identify Port Blair as the 13th major port reflect an earlier classification.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the current and older classifications.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s major ports:
1. India has 12 operational major ports.
2. Vadhavan is included as the 13th major port after its approval in 2024.
3. India has approximately 200 non-major ports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The current count is 13 major ports including Vadhavan, of which 12 are operational, and India has about 200 non-major ports.
accepted.tq: Check the current count against the operational count and the broader category.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: New Mangalore Port — Gulf of Khambhat
accepted.x: Deendayal Port is located in Gujarat on the Gulf of Kachchh. The other ports are associated with Goa, Kerala and Karnataka respectively, not the water bodies mentioned.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure port–location pair.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The special significance of Deendayal (Kandla) Port is that it was
o: built after the loss of Karachi and had Asia’s first export processing zone
the first corporatised major port of India
the only riverine major port of India
accepted.x: Deendayal Port was built after the loss of Karachi, and Asia’s first Export Processing Zone was established at Kandla in 1965.
accepted.tq: Use the speciality rather than merely the state or coast.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which major port is India’s first 100 per cent landlord major port and the largest container port?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), also known as Nhava Sheva, is India’s largest container port and its first 100 per cent landlord major port.
accepted.tq: Identify the port from two distinctive specialities.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vadhavan Port is proposed as a greenfield deep-draft port through a special purpose vehicle in which JNPA and the Maharashtra Maritime Board hold shares in the ratio of
accepted.x: The Vadhavan Port SPV is owned 74 per cent by JNPA and 26 per cent by the Maharashtra Maritime Board. The project cost is estimated at Rs 76,220 crore and it is due in 2034.
accepted.tq: Test the exact numerical shareholding rather than a rounded ratio.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vadhavan major port is located in which district of Maharashtra?
accepted.x: Vadhavan Port is located in Palghar district of Maharashtra. It is a greenfield, deep-draft major port.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the district from nearby coastal districts.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following ports is correctly matched with its speciality?
1. Mumbai — natural harbour with a wet dock
2. Mormugao — natural harbour in the Zuari estuary
3. New Mangalore — artificial lagoon port
4. Kochi — natural port in the Vembanad region
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairings are correct. Mumbai is a natural harbour with a wet dock; Mormugao lies in the Zuari estuary; New Mangalore is an artificial lagoon port; and Kochi is a natural port associated with Vembanad.
accepted.tq: Verify each port–speciality pair independently.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: New Mangalore Port is particularly associated with the export of
accepted.x: New Mangalore Port in Karnataka exports Kudremukh iron ore. The other minerals and regions are not the speciality stated for this port.
accepted.tq: Link the port with its distinctive export commodity.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the ports of Tamil Nadu?
1. VOC Tuticorin is an artificial all-weather harbour.
2. Chennai is the oldest artificial port on the east coast.
3. Kamarajar is the first corporatised major port.
4. All three are major ports of Tamil Nadu.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Tamil Nadu has the three major ports of Chennai, Kamarajar and VOC Tuticorin; their respective specialities are also correctly stated.
accepted.tq: Use a complete state-wise port cluster and check each speciality.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: VOC Tuticorin Port is located
o: south of the Palk Strait and east of Adam’s Bridge
north of Adam’s Bridge on the eastern coast
accepted.x: VOC Tuticorin is an artificial all-weather harbour situated north of Adam’s Bridge on the east coast of India.
accepted.tq: Test the precise geographical location using a nearby physical feature.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the only riverine major port of India?
accepted.x: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, comprising Kolkata-Haldia, is the oldest major port and the only riverine major port of India. It is situated on the Hooghly.
accepted.tq: Identify the unique exception in the port classification.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Visakhapatnam Port is distinguished as India’s
o: oldest artificial port on the east coast
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh is described as the deepest landlocked, protected harbour in India.
accepted.tq: Match a unique superlative with its port.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Paradip Port was declared a major port on 18 April 1966. It is notable for being
o: the first major port on the east coast after Independence
the first landlord port in western India
the first major port established before Independence
accepted.x: Paradip was declared a major port on 18 April 1966 and was the first major port on the east coast established after Independence.
accepted.tq: Combine the exact date with the associated historical distinction.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: VOC Tuticorin is an artificial all-weather harbour, not a natural harbour. Deendayal is tidal, Kamarajar was the first corporatised major port, and Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked protected harbour.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed speciality in the port–feature pairs.
accepted.sec: Major ports → state, coast and speciality  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, how many National Waterways were declared?
accepted.x: The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 National Waterways. This statutory number is distinct from the number currently operational.
accepted.tq: Separate the total declared waterways from the operational count.
accepted.sec: National Waterways → route, terminals, number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes National Waterway-2?
o: Kollam–Kottapuram on the West Coast Canal
Kakinada–Puducherry through the Godavari and Krishna canals
accepted.x: National Waterway-2 extends from Dhubri to Sadiya for 891 km on the Brahmaputra. The other alternatives describe NW-1, NW-3 and NW-4 respectively.
accepted.tq: Match the waterway number with its route and river system.
accepted.sec: National Waterways → route, terminals, number  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following National Waterways in ascending order of their stated length:
A. NW-1
B. NW-2
C. NW-3
D. NW-4
accepted.x: The lengths are NW-3: 205 km, NW-2: 891 km, NW-4: 1,095 km and NW-1: 1,620 km. Therefore, the order is C, B, D, A.
accepted.tq: Arrange by numerical length, checking the smallest and largest first.
accepted.sec: National Waterways → route, terminals, number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: National Waterway-5 is associated with which of the following routes and water systems?
o: Talcher/Angul–Paradip/Dhamra; Brahmani-Mahanadi and East Coast Canal
accepted.x: NW-5 covers Talcher or Angul to Paradip or Dhamra and involves the Brahmani-Mahanadi system and the East Coast Canal in Odisha and West Bengal.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the eastern canal route from the west-coast route.
accepted.sec: National Waterways → route, terminals, number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The target for inland waterway cargo by 2030 is
accepted.x: The target is 200 million metric tonnes by 2030. Inland waterway cargo had risen from 18 MMT in 2013–14 to 146 MMT in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Identify the forward target rather than the historical base figure.
accepted.sec: National Waterways → route, terminals, number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which port became the largest cargo-handling port according to the 2026 ranking cited?
accepted.x: Paradip is the current largest cargo-handling port in the cited 2026 ranking. Deendayal was the earlier answer used in the APPSC 2019 key.
accepted.tq: Separate the current ranking from an older examination key.
accepted.sec: Port traffic rankings - top cargo handler, container ports, states with most major ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Major ports handled approximately how much cargo in 2025–26?
accepted.x: Major ports handled 915.17 million tonnes in 2025–26, exceeding the target of 904 million tonnes by 7.06 per cent year on year.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the achieved quantity from the target quantity.
accepted.sec: Port traffic rankings - top cargo handler, container ports, states with most major ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding port traffic rankings:
1. JNPA is India’s largest container port.
2. Paradip led dry bulk in LPPI 2024–25.
3. Sikka led liquid bulk in LPPI 2024–25.
4. Mundra led container cargo in LPPI 2024–25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. JNPA is the largest container port overall, while the LPPI category leaders were Paradip for dry bulk, Sikka for liquid bulk and Mundra for container cargo.
accepted.tq: Separate the overall port ranking from category-wise cargo leaders.
accepted.sec: Port traffic rankings - top cargo handler, container ports, states with most major ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the World Bank’s CPPI 2024, which of the following is correct regarding Indian ports?
o: Two Indian ports were in the top 30 and seven were in the top 100.
No Indian port was in the top 100.
Seven Indian ports were in the top 30 and two were in the top 100.
Two Indian ports were in the top 10 and seven were in the top 30.
accepted.x: The CPPI 2024 placed two Indian ports in the global top 30 and seven Indian ports in the top 100. The container turnaround time cited is about 30 hours.
accepted.tq: Check the nested ranking categories carefully.
accepted.sec: Port traffic rankings - top cargo handler, container ports, states with most major ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which States have three major ports when the current Vadhavan classification is taken into account?
accepted.x: Tamil Nadu has Chennai, Kamarajar and VOC Tuticorin. With Vadhavan counted, Maharashtra has Mumbai, JNPA and Vadhavan.
accepted.tq: Compare state-wise port counts after applying the current classification.
accepted.sec: Port traffic rankings - top cargo handler, container ports, states with most major ports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first airmail flight in India, on 18 February 1911, operated between
accepted.x: India’s first airmail flight was operated from Allahabad to Naini on 18 February 1911.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact inaugural route and date together.
accepted.sec: Civil aviation - first flight, nationalisation, green airports, UDAN, busiest  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Air transport in India was nationalised in 1953 under the Air Corporations Act, which created
o: Indian Airlines and Air India International
Air India International and Alliance Air
accepted.x: The Air Corporations Act, 1953 nationalised air transport and created Indian Airlines and Air India International.
accepted.tq: Match the legislation with the entities created by it.
accepted.sec: Civil aviation - first flight, nationalisation, green airports, UDAN, busiest  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The number of operational airports in India increased from 74 in 2014 to approximately what number in 2025?
accepted.x: Operational airports increased from 74 in 2014 to 164 in 2025. India is also identified as the world’s third-largest domestic aviation market.
accepted.tq: Test the change between the base year and the latest stated year.
accepted.sec: Civil aviation - first flight, nationalisation, green airports, UDAN, busiest  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes UDAN?
o: It is a cargo-only scheme without passenger routes.
It was launched in 1953 under the Air Corporations Act.
It means Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik and operates with viability gap funding.
It means Universal Domestic Aviation Network and is financed only through airport taxes.
accepted.x: UDAN stands for Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik and operates through viability gap funding. It was launched in 2016.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and identify the operating mechanism.
accepted.sec: Civil aviation - first flight, nationalisation, green airports, UDAN, busiest  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding UDAN:
1. It was launched in 2016.
2. Of 663 routes launched since 2017, 327 had been discontinued by February 2026.
3. Modified UDAN is scheduled to run from 2026–27 to 2035–36.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. UDAN began in 2016; 327 of 663 routes had been discontinued by February 2026; and Modified UDAN is scheduled for FY 2026–27 to 2035–36.
accepted.tq: Track the scheme’s launch, performance figure and modified phase separately.
accepted.sec: Civil aviation - first flight, nationalisation, green airports, UDAN, busiest  [APPSC]
